This is not a cause-effect relationship but an identity statement: the thought-of-expecting-to-cry IS, in its essential nature, just another species of alien thought. It belongs to the evil/obstruction polarity because it disrupts the wholeness of prayer. Since there are zero dataset edges for this Torah, no package exists to assign it to.

analysis_notes.gap_analysis_summary: Torah #95 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan Tinyana — five sentences on the proper way to conduct hitbodedut (personal prayer/meditation), saying Tehillim, supplications, and requests before God. The teaching has NO entries in torahData.js at reference 1095 — the dataset is completely empty for this Torah. Reading the source text carefully reveals exactly one explicit bechina equivalence: the thought of anticipating weeping during prayer (מחשבת הבכי / ציפייה לבכיה) is declared a bechina of מחשבה זרה (alien thought that disrupts kavvanah). This is a clear identity statement ('הוּא גַּם-כֵּן בְּחִינַת מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה'). The remaining concepts in the teaching — hitbodedut, saying of Tehillim/supplications/requests, speaking with a whole heart, weeping before God as a child before a father, focusing on the words of prayer, speaking as a man to his friend — are described functionally and are connected by eitza (cause-and-effect) rather than bechina. For example: speaking the words without alien thoughts (eitza) → the heart is aroused → weeping. These are not bechina equivalences and do not belong in a bechina package. The missing bechina pair (ציפייה לבכיה ↔ מחשבה זרה) would form a two-node 'evil obstruction' package if entered into the dataset, but since only two nodes are present it does not meet the threshold for a new full package proposal (see torah_95_new_packages.json).
